answer.rationale: Rollback is compliance-blocked despite memory_b1's clean precedent, so it's excluded outright. The write-path latency climb coincides with peak settlement load, closely matching memory_b3's precedent where provisioning headroom absorbed a peak-driven surge without queue growth. Regional failover (memory_b2) carries risk of dropping in-flight writes during a failover cutover, conflicting with the 'no lost writes' objective, so I want its archived record checked before ruling it out. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing address different failure modes (dependency outages, read-heavy contention) rather than raw write-path capacity exhaustion under peak load, so they're less directly applicable here. Add_capacity lets me relieve write-path pressure without touching the protected release, preserving the security patch while buying headroom during peak settlement traffic.
